public_rationale: Anthropic's October 26, 2026 filing reports an $8.3 billion net loss for the year ended December 31, 2024 [e1]. A July 2, 2025 report describes Surge AI as profitable since its founding in 2020, but supplies no net-income amount or accounting definition [e2]. These examples do not establish whether more than half of the relevant companies had negative net income in their latest reporting periods applicable to the June 30, 2025 observation [e1, e2].
limitations: The packet establishes neither a defined company population nor comparable net-income results for enough companies to determine a majority.
Surge's reported profitability is not supported by a comparable primary net-income disclosure in the packet.
Cash burn, operating losses, revenue and fundraising cannot substitute for net-income results.
The product-market-fit language has no measurable duration or threshold, and the qualified valuation judgment supplies no numerical test.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI companies are predominantly unprofitable, perpetually searching for product-market fit, and even when they find it seem incapable of generating revenue that remotely justifies their valuations.

statement.excerpt: These companies are predominantly unprofitable, perpetually searching for product-market fit, and even when they find it, seem incapable of generating revenue numbers that remotely justify their valuations.

from_speaker: revenue numbers that remotely justify their valuations
our_interpretation: The testable core is that most of the generative AI companies under discussion were losing money around publication. 'Predominantly' ordinarily means more than half, counting companies equally.
The surrounding revenue discussion supplies the relevant population. It does not supply an exhaustive company list or a precise boundary between generative AI businesses and their suppliers.
I read 'unprofitable' as having negative net income. Cash burn, operating losses and negative gross margins are not interchangeable with net losses.

For this ongoing June 2025 observation, use each company's latest reported annual or interim results relevant to its position before publication. The reporting window includes calendar 2024, the latest completed annual period, and available 2025 interim periods through June 30. It is not restricted to the first quarter of 2025.
The surrounding reliance on press-reported financial figures implies an estimate basis; the speaker specifies no accounting standard.

'Perpetually searching' describes a continuing difficulty finding durable customer demand. It does not establish a measurable duration or mean that no company has customers: the next clause expressly allows that some find product-market fit.

'Seem incapable' and 'remotely justify' express a qualified valuation judgment. I will not turn them into a firm revenue multiple, a prediction of permanent failure, or an independently scored assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable company-level evidence establishes negative net income for more than half of the relevant companies in their latest reporting periods applicable to the June 2025 observation. A few prominent loss-making companies are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that at least half of the relevant companies were profitable or breaking even in those periods. Individual profitable exceptions do not contradict 'predominantly'.

evidence.locator: Risk Factors, page 64; accompanying historical loss paragraph; financial statement audit report, page F-4
evidence.publisher: Anthropic, PBC / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence.explanation: The accompanying paragraph reports an $8.3 billion net loss for 2024, and the filing includes audited statements for that year. This establishes a relevant loss-making example, but one company's result cannot establish the proportion of companies losing money.

evidence.locator: Historical revenue paragraph; preceding paragraph on profitability since inception
evidence.publisher: GlobalData / Verdict, syndicated by Yahoo Finance
evidence.explanation: This Reuters-based account reports substantial realized revenue and separately describes Surge as profitable since inception. It is a relevant exception and evidence of commercial demand, but gives no net-income amount or accounting definition; it cannot disprove a majority claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A population defined independently of profitability, with comparable net-income results for each company's latest applicable annual or interim period through June 30, 2025. Counting each company once and leaving undisclosed results unknown, the evidence must establish either that more than half had net losses or that at least half were profitable or breaking even.
